The parentheses are mismatched, making the actual call `hashlib.sha256(...string...).encode("utf-8").hexdigest()` — but `sha256()` takes bytes, not a str. **TypeError at runtime** if `APP_SECRET` and `SESSION_SECRET` are both empty.[1]

16. `infer_date_filters`: the `end = (now if year == now.year else datetime(year, 12, 31, 23, 59, 59, 999000, tzinfo=timezone.utc)` expression is not closed with `)`, **SyntaxError**.[1]
17. `run_exa_search`: `search_type = ("auto" if include_domains or len(queries) > 1 or any(k in lowered for k in [...])` — the `any(` and outer ternary parentheses are not properly closed, **SyntaxError**.[1]
18. `run_exa_search`: `all_sources.append({"index":..., ...` — the `append({` call is never closed with `})`, **SyntaxError**.[1]
19. `run_exa_search`: after all queries are exhausted, if `all_sources` is non-empty but `last_error` is also set (partial failure), **no warning is returned to the caller** — silent partial failure, **logical error**.[1]
20. `map_images_for_flymyai`: payload is pre-populated with keys `"image"` through `"image13"` (14 slots), but the loop only iterates `image_uploads[:14]` — index 0 maps to `"image"` (no number), indices 1–13 map to `"image1"`–`"image13"`. That means the dict defines `"image1"` through `"image13"` (13 numbered keys) plus `"image"`, totalling 14 — **but** the pre-populated payload also contains `"image1"` through `"image13"` which is 13 entries plus `"image"` = 14. However the loop goes up to index 13 (0-based), using key `f"image{idx}"` for idx=13 → `"image13"`. The pre-defined dict has `"image13": None`, so this is consistent. However `idx` starts at 0, and `key = "image" if idx == 0 else f"image{idx}"` — idx=1 → `"image1"`, ..., idx=13 → `"image13"`. The pre-populated dict has keys `"image1"` through `"image13"` — **not** `"image2"` through `"image13"` and a separate `"image1"`. This is consistent but the pre-population includes `None` for all 14 keys unconditionally, meaning **unused image slots are sent as `None`** to the API, which may cause unexpected API-side errors.[1]
21. `run_flymyai_image_generation`: `payload` includes `"aspect_ratio": None` and `"image_size": None` — these are passed as explicit `None` values to the model API, which may not accept null fields and could **cause API errors**.[1]
22. `build_model_messages`: `recent_messages = chat.messages[-12:]` — `chat.messages` is a SQLAlchemy relationship loaded lazily; if the session is expired or detached, this will raise a **DetachedInstanceError**.[1]
23. `build_model_messages`: the `system_content` is built as `"\n".join((...))` where the inner argument is a **bare tuple** (missing `[` `]` or explicit tuple comma syntax makes it a generator expression without `[]`). Actually it's a multi-line parenthesized string concatenation — Python will implicitly concatenate adjacent string literals inside `()`, resulting in a single long string, **not** a joined list. The `"\n".join()` call will then iterate over **individual characters** of that single string, joining them with `\n`. This is a critical **logical error** — the system prompt will be broken into individual characters separated by newlines.[1]
24. `send_message`: `upload_ids = list(dict.fromkeys([int(x) for x in body.upload_ids if int(x) > 0]))` — `int(x)` is called **twice** per element (once in the filter condition, once in the value), which is redundant and a **performance/style error**.[1]
25. `send_message`: `recent_messages[:-1]` is passed to `run_exa_search` — this excludes the last message in the list, but at this point the newly added `user_message` has already been committed and may appear in the query result. The intent is presumably to exclude the current message from context, but if the query returns the newly saved message, `recent_messages[:-1]` would **incorrectly exclude the second-to-last message** instead.[1]
26. `send_message` (image mode): `assistant_content = content` — the assistant message content is set to the **user's prompt**, not to any meaningful AI-generated text or description of the image. This means the assistant message will just echo the prompt back, which is **logically wrong**.[1]
27. `chat.updated_at = datetime.utcnow()` is called in multiple places using `datetime.utcnow()` — this function is **deprecated since Python 3.12** and returns a naive datetime. The column `updated_at` has `onupdate=datetime.utcnow` (non-callable reference, correct for SQLAlchemy), but the manual assignments use `datetime.utcnow()` (naive), while `serialize_message` and `chat_preview` call `.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` assuming UTC — **inconsistency** between naive and timezone-aware datetime handling throughout the codebase.[1]
28. `User.created_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow, ...)` — `datetime.utcnow` is passed as a reference (not called), which is correct for SQLAlchemy defaults, but `datetime.utcnow` is deprecated in Python 3.12+. Should use `lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc)` or `datetime.now` with timezone.[1]
29. `decode_session_token` has no type annotation for its return value beyond `dict`, and never handles the case where `serializer.loads` raises exceptions other than `BadSignature` / `SignatureExpired`. The caller in `get_current_user` only catches those two, so any **other exception** from `loads` (e.g., `json.JSONDecodeError`) propagates as an unhandled 500 error.[1]
30. `get_current_user`: `int(payload.get("user_id", 0))` — if `payload["user_id"]` is not castable to int (e.g., a malformed token), this raises an **unhandled ValueError**, resulting in a 500 error instead of a proper 401.[1]
31. `json_loads_safe`: if `json.loads(value)` returns a non-list JSON value (e.g., a dict or integer), the function silently returns `[]` with no error or log. This swallows valid but unexpected JSON structures — **silent data loss**.[1]
32. `extract_text_from_file`: at the end of the function, there is an unconditional `return ""` after the `try/except` block, which is **unreachable** because all branches inside the `try` already return. This dead code is a **logic/style error**.[1]
33. `compress_query`: deduplication is done with `if token not in kept` using a list, giving **O(n²)** complexity. Should use a set for O(1) lookup.[1]
34. `compress_query`: `kept[:12]` limits to 12 tokens, but the function is also called in `generate_exa_queries` where `base.split()[:8]` is used. The two limits (12 and 8) are inconsistent and not documented.[1]
35. `generate_exa_queries`: `user_history[-2:]` plus `[base]` are joined, but `base` is already the last user message, so if `user_history` already ends with `base`, it will be **duplicated in the combo query**.[1]
36. `generate_exa_queries`: returns at most 4 queries (`deduped[:4]`), but `run_exa_search` loops over all returned queries with a `break` at 20 results — if there are fewer than 4 queries and each returns fewer than 20 results, the cap of 20 may never be reached, potentially making fewer API calls than needed. Not strictly an error but a **design inconsistency**.[1]
37. `run_exa_search`: `kwargs` dict uses `"type"` as a key, but the Exa Python SDK's `search()` method parameter is `type` (positional or keyword). Passing it as `**kwargs` with key `"type"` should work, but `"type"` is also a Python built-in name — while not a runtime error, it's a **naming collision risk and style issue**.[1]
38. `run_exa_search`: `"extras": {"links": 1}` — passing `1` (integer) as the value for `"links"` inside `extras`. If the API expects a boolean or specific structure, this could cause **unexpected API behavior**.[1]
39. `run_exa_search`: `if len(all_sources) >= 20: break` appears **twice** (once inside the inner for-loop and once after it). The inner break only exits the inner `for item in ...` loop, not the outer `for query in queries` loop — the outer break is needed and correctly placed, but the inner one only limits results **per query**, not globally before the outer loop continues to the next query. This means results could exceed 20 if the count hits exactly 20 on the inner check then the outer loop runs again before the outer check. Actually checking: inner loop appends then checks `>= 20` and breaks inner loop; then outer loop immediately checks `>= 20` and breaks — this is actually correct but redundant and confusing.[1]
40. `compact_sources_for_prompt`: `source.get("title") or source.get("url")` — if both are empty strings or `None`, the result is `None`, and `f"[{i}] {title}\nURL: {url}\n..."` will render as `[1] None\nURL: \n...` — **None** printed as literal string.[1]
41. `build_file_context`: `budget = 24000` and `used += len(clip)` — `len(clip)` counts **bytes of a Python str** (characters, not bytes). For multi-byte characters (e.g., Hungarian text), actual byte size is larger. The budget is described as a character count but may be intended as a token/byte budget — **inconsistency**.[1]
42. `build_file_context`: `remaining = max(budget - used, 0)` then `clip = text[:remaining]` — if `remaining == 0`, `clip = text[:0] = ""`, and `entries.append(header + "")` appends a header with no content. Then `used += 0`, so subsequent uploads also get `remaining == 0`. This means once the budget is exhausted, all remaining uploads still get their **header appended with no content**, potentially cluttering the prompt.[1]
43. `run_friendli_chat`: `model="zai-org/GLM-5"` — this model name contains a slash which is unusual for API model identifiers. If this is not a valid model identifier on the Friendli API, **all chat calls will fail** with an API error.[1]
44. `run_friendli_chat`: `completion.choices[0].message` — no check that `completion.choices` is non-empty. If the API returns zero choices, this raises an **IndexError**.[1]
45. `store_generated_image`: `file_path.write_bytes(image_bytes)` — no error handling. If the disk is full or permissions are denied, an **unhandled OSError** propagates as a 500 error with no cleanup.[1]
46. `upload_file` endpoint: `out.close()` is called explicitly inside the `with` block before `file_path.unlink()` — this is redundant because the `with` statement will close the file, and manually calling `close()` inside a `with` block is a **style/logic error** (though not harmful).[1]
47. `upload_file` endpoint: `text_content=text_content[:120000] if text_content else None` — the cap of 120,000 characters is applied **after** `extract_text_from_file` already caps PDF extraction at 40,000 characters. For text files there is no cap inside the extractor, so only the DB insertion cap of 120,000 applies — **inconsistent limits** between file types.[1]
48. `get_upload` endpoint: `FileResponse` is returned with both `filename=upload.original_name` and a manual `Content-Disposition` header — **duplicate/conflicting** disposition headers may be sent, since `FileResponse` already sets `Content-Disposition` based on the `filename` parameter.[1]
49. `send_message`: `for upload in uploads: upload.chat_id = chat.id` — this modifies uploads that may belong to other chats (i.e., uploads previously associated with a different chat). There is no check whether `upload.chat_id` is already set to a different value, causing **silent reassignment of chat ownership**.[1]
50. `send_message`: `is_first_user_message` check queries the DB for the count of user messages **before** the new `user_message` is committed. If this endpoint is called concurrently for the same chat, both requests could get `count == 0` and both would set `chat.title`, leading to a **race condition** in title assignment.[1]
51. `register` endpoint: after `db.commit()` for the user, a `Chat` is created and `db.commit()` is called again — but `db.refresh(user)` is called **before** the chat commit, meaning the refreshed user object does not reflect the new chat in its `chats` relationship if it was lazy-loaded earlier. Minor inconsistency but could cause **stale relationship data**.[1]
52. `login` endpoint: no rate limiting or account lockout logic — **not** listed as a security concern per instructions, but it is a **missing feature / logical gap** in authentication flow.[1]
53. `clean_env`: `if value is None: return default` — this branch is **unreachable** because `os.getenv(name, default)` with a non-None `default` never returns `None`. The `None` check is dead code.[1]
54. `clean_env`: the quote-stripping logic only strips matching single or double quotes at position `[0]` and `[-1]`, but does **not** handle mixed quotes (e.g., `'"value'`) — would incorrectly strip in that case since it only checks that both ends match the same quote type. Actually re-reading: it checks `value[0] == "'"` AND `value[-1] == "'"` (same type), so mixed quotes are not stripped. This is correct, but the logic doesn't handle nested or escaped quotes — minor **incompleteness**.[1]
55. `serialize_upload`: `upload.created_at.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc).isoformat()` — if `created_at` is already timezone-aware (e.g., if the DB driver returns tz-aware datetimes), `.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` will **overwrite** the existing tzinfo without conversion, potentially producing incorrect timestamps.[1]
56. `serialize_message`: same issue as #55 — `message.created_at.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc).isoformat()` assumes naive datetime.[1]
57. `chat_preview`: same issue as #55 — `chat.created_at.replace(...)` and `chat.updated_at.replace(...)` assume naive datetimes.[1]
58. `infer_date_filters`: `years = [int(y) for y in re.findall(r"\b(20\d{2})\b", message)]` — this finds all 4-digit years starting with `20`. If the user message contains a year like `2099` or `2000`, it will be included. No validation that the year is reasonable (e.g., not in the future beyond the current year). **Logical gap**.[1]
59. `infer_date_filters`: when `len(years) >= 2`, `year1 = min(years)` and `year2 = max(years)` — if the same year appears twice in the text, `year1 == year2` and the range `datetime(year1,1,1)` to `datetime(year2,12,31,...)` would span a full single year, which may not match user intent. **Edge case logical error**.[1]
60. `extract_domains`: `re.findall(r"(?:https?://)?(?:www\.)?([a-zA-Z0-9-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})(?:/[\S]*)?", text)` — the outer group captures only the domain without path, but the regex also matches plain words containing a dot (e.g., `"e.g."`, `"i.e."`, version numbers like `"v1.0"`). This could **add spurious domains** to `include_domains`.[1]
61. `extract_domains`: `domain = match.lower().strip(".,)")` — `.strip(".,)")` strips these characters from both ends of the domain. A domain ending in `)` is valid in some text contexts (e.g., `example.com)`) but stripping could also remove legitimate trailing characters in edge cases. Minor robustness issue.[1]
62. `run_exa_search`: date filter keys (`start_published_date`, etc.) are passed directly as `kwargs[key] = value` — if the Exa SDK does not accept these as top-level keyword arguments to `search()`, this will raise a **TypeError**. The Exa SDK API should be verified.[1]
63. `map_images_for_flymyai`: `file_path = UPLOAD_DIR / upload.stored_name` then `if not file_path.exists(): continue` — if the file doesn't exist, it is silently skipped. No error is raised, no log is written. The caller `run_flymyai_image_generation` will not know that an image was missing — **silent data loss**.[1]
64. `run_flymyai_image_generation`: `output_data.get("image")` — if the output contains the image under a different key (e.g., `"output"`, `"result"`, `"images"`), this will always return `None` and raise a 500 error. **Fragile key assumption**.[1]
65. `send_message` (chat mode): `recent_messages` is fetched **after** `user_message` is committed to DB, so `recent_messages` includes the current user message. Then `recent_messages[:-1]` is passed to `run_exa_search`, excluding the last message (the current one). But `build_model_messages` uses `chat.messages[-12:]` which is loaded from the relationship — this may or may not include the freshly committed message depending on session state and `expire_on_commit=False`. **Inconsistent message context** between search and model.[1]
66. `build_model_messages`: `for message in recent_messages: if message.role not in {"user", "assistant"}: continue` — this silently skips messages with unexpected roles. There is no validation when messages are saved that `role` must be `"user"` or `"assistant"`. A message saved with role `"system"` would be silently ignored.[1]
67. `ChatMessageBody.mode`: default is `"chat"`, validated in `send_message` against `{"chat", "image"}`. However, the validation is `if mode not in {"chat", "image"}: raise HTTPException(...)` — this is correct, but there is no Pydantic validator on the model itself, so invalid `mode` values are only caught at runtime inside the endpoint, not at request parsing time. **Missing Pydantic field validator**.[1]
68. `ChatMessageBody.content`: default is `""` (empty string). Combined with `content = body.content.strip()`, an all-whitespace message will pass Pydantic validation and only be caught by the `if mode == "chat" and not content and not uploads` check. Fine, but Pydantic-level `min_length` validation is **missing** for content.[1]
69. `send_message`: `upload_ids = list(dict.fromkeys([int(x) for x in body.upload_ids if int(x) > 0]))` — upload IDs of `0` are silently filtered out with no error or feedback to the client. If a client sends `upload_ids=[0]` expecting it to be processed, it will be silently dropped.[1]
70. `compress_query`: `re.findall(r"[\wáéíóöőúüűÁÉÍÓÖŐÚÜŰ.-]+", text.lower())` — the character class includes `.` and `-` which can match standalone dots and hyphens, creating tokens like `"."` or `"-"`. These pass the `len(token) < 3` filter (they're length 1), so they're filtered out — but `"v1.0"` would become token `"v1.0"` with length 4 and could be included as a query keyword. Minor issue.[1]

**That's all.**
